recipes.name: Angel's Chunky Chicken Salad
ingredients_raw: 1 cooked, boneless chicken breast half, chopped

steps.text: Combine the chicken, celery, mayonnaise, onion and pickle; mix well.
Season with the garlic powder, salt and pepper. Serve with lettuce on fresh crusty bread or bun.

raw_recipe.headline: Angel's Chunky Chicken Salad
raw_recipe.description: I made up this recipe after a similar sandwich served at a diner. It's not the same, but just as good.

review.reviewBody: Very good "basic" chicken salad that you can but in your own additions based on your tastes. I made this for my husband to take to work, so no additions needed. I used a bit more mayo and used a bit of onion powder vs. onion. And, like others I used sweet pickle relish vs. chopping dill pickles. I put this into a tortilla along with some lettuce, tomato and a couple of slices of bacon for a really good wrap sandwich.

Great chicken salad! I switched the pickle for apple, added a small amount of crushed pecans, and 2 teaspoons of sugar (it makes a huge difference, but you don’t actually taste it). I also added some tarragon to flesh out the flavor a little more.

Make a big batch and freeze what you’re not going to eat soon. It’s great for making meal preps. Bread’s cool, but a scoop or two of this on top of some mixed greens is where it’s at!

by itself I'm sure this was great, but since my pregnancy hormones are everywhere and I was craving some roasted red bell peppers and a little spice I modified a bit. I boiled the chicken with roasted red bell peppers, the ends of one celery, garlic powder, pepper and sea salt. For the salad I pureed one big roasted bell pepper strip and 3 cloves of garlic with pepper and italian seasoning. In the bowl I mixed the puree, 1 celery stalk chopped finely, 1 tsp of sweet relish, 1 dill sandwich stacker chopped finely, 1/2 of a red onion chopped, and about 3 tbsp of mayo, I stuck in the freezer for about 20 min to chill it and then served it on croissants with tomato and avocados, it was delicious. Thanks so much for sharing your recipe without it I wasn't sure where to start but with it I made something great and something that I will have to keep making bc the baby loved it.

This recipe was so easy! I made this for a baby shower and served it on croissants with romaine lettuce - was a HUGE hit. I adjusted the recipe for 14 people and then did the onion and pickles to taste - it called for 3-1/2 onions - YIKES! I baked the chicken breast with poultry seasoning, garlic salt and pepper then shredded and chopped a little. Instead of using garlic powder I used the claussen dill pickles that have garlic in them. I will definitely make this again.

This chicken salad recipe is good with dill pickle relish, fresh garlic, chopped grapes and pecans, and Old Bay seasoning in place of salt and pepper. I used rotisserie chicken, and used the rest to make chicken stock.

This is a fairly standard base for chicken salad but it needs customization for your own tastes. We add finely diced Fuji apple and walnuts and occasionally halved grapes to it to add crunch and a sweet note. Occasionally we replace half the mayo with Miracle Whip.

so I doubled everything and found that I needed about 9T of mayo, rather than the 6 that doubling would have called for. I also added more garlic powder (twice what doubling would have called for). It needed something extra so I added 3/4 diced green pepper. Might try a yellow or red pepper next time, but overall, good.

Basic and simple just like a chicken salad should be. I made exactly as written and thought this was pretty good. It was pretty pickle forward so def use a pickle you are familiar with and like. Next time I might try cutting back on the pickles so that I can add a little yellow mustard. It would have been too salty for both. I'll also probably use a red onion to give it some color. Overall good recipe and one that can easily be changed to suit your taste or what you have on hand.
This was very good with a modification. I doubled the chicken, onion and mayo, plus an extra tablespoon of mayo for more creaminess, also added a touch of pickle juice to mayo.
I used Frichik rather than real chicken. Delicious!!!

I think this is an awesome recipe! I made it for the first time yesterday and it came out great. I made some changes... I added small apple chunks, used chicken breast tenders, and basically added all the ingredients to my taste (just threw everything in slowly and added more/less as I saw fit), I only used one dill pickle (because I know they have a suck strong taste), and probably less onion and celery than the recipe called for and I was very happy with it. I also used Light Miracle Whip for the mayo, which gave a kind of zesty taste and put it on toasted wheat bread with lettuce. The end result, I feel, was still missing that special something that really makes it pop, but overall... great recipe! Very basic and I think anyone would like it, you can't really go wrong. Thanks for sharing!
I did not think I would like chicken salad, my first time eating and it was wonderfully and surprisingly good.

I had two large chicken breasts worth of meat so I had to increase the other ingredients proportionately. I used a whole sweet onion, left out the pickles (didn't have any) and substituted some blue cheese dressing for mayo. Enjoyed by all.
So tasty! Simple and elegant.
Great taste. I made tea sandwiches. I used canned chicken and added sweet relish to this and everyone enjoyed it!
I increased the chicken and mayo, less onion...very good!
Subbed sweet relish/bread & butter pickles
I have made this twice now and both times it came out great. I will make this again.
Turns out great. Obviously you can adjust based on flavor you like. I added a little more mayo and garlic powder.
Absolutely delicious! I used leftover turkey from Thanksgiving. I left out the pickles and added a bit more mayonnaise. I will definitely make this again.
